prompt:
The batch cannot go to the buyer until the marking on the glove has been checked against the type-test report, so the sample is laid out under the bench lamp.

A cut-resistant glove lies back uppermost on the sample table, the shield mark and its row of figures on the back of the hand. The type-test report is spread out flat beside it and lists its results in the laboratory's own running order: tear 44 newtons, puncture 118 newtons, abrasion 6200 cycles, blade cut index 3.4. The marking rule sets the places under the shield in a different order, abrasion, blade cut, tear, puncture. The banding tables are alongside: abrasion steps at 100, 500, 2000 and 8000 cycles; blade cut at 1.2, 2.5, 5.0 and 10.0; tear at 10, 25, 50 and 75 newtons; puncture at 20, 60, 100 and 150 newtons, each step passed lifting the mark by a place.

What the row of figures under the shield has to read is what the report does not print.
easy_question: Does this picture show a protective glove lying back uppermost on a sample table with a shield mark on the back of the hand and a printed test report spread out beside it? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Look at the row of figures stamped under the shield mark on the back of the glove and read the figure standing in the first place. Answer with one of: the first place holds 3; the first place holds 2; the first place holds 4.

Look at the same row of figures under the shield mark and read the figure standing in the third place, counting from the left. Answer with one of: the third place holds 2; the third place holds 3; the third place holds 4.
